name: Celestia

seo.title: Celestia Phinisi Yacht Charter: Raja Ampat & Komodo
seo.description: Celestia, a 45m hand-built phinisi with 7 staterooms for 14 guests, charters Raja Ampat, Komodo and the Spice Islands, whole yacht only, from US$13,500 a night.

tagline: A 45-metre phinisi for fourteen, chartered whole: Raja Ampat, Komodo and the Spice Islands
answer: Celestia is a 45-metre phinisi hand-built by Bulukumba craftsmen and launched in 2023, with seven en-suite staterooms over four decks for up to 14 guests and a crew of 17. She is chartered whole only: Komodo May to September, the Spice Islands in April and September to October, Raja Ampat October to April. She suits families and private groups who want diving with Nitrox.
facts: Dive room, dive master aboard, Nitrox for certified divers
Speedboats aboard; water toys incl. water skis, wakeboard, underwater scooter
Deirdre Renniers, Singapore and Cape Town
overview: Celestia is a 45-metre phinisi, custom designed and built by hand by the boat builders of Bulukumba in South Sulawesi, and launched in 2023. She sails the Indonesian archipelago with seven staterooms for 14 guests and a crew of 17, including an expedition leader and a dive master.

The staterooms sit on three decks: a Master on the main deck, two Owner's staterooms with private terraces on the upper deck, and four Deluxe staterooms on the lower deck, two with queen beds and two with twins. Every one has its own bathroom. Above them is a rooftop sun lounge; the saloon, dining area and dive room are on the main deck.

She follows the seasons: Raja Ampat from October to April, Komodo, Sumbawa and Alor from May to September, and the Spice Islands of the Banda Sea on the crossings in April and from September to October. Each charter is the whole yacht, with the route drawn around the group.
why: She is sold one way: the whole yacht, crewed and catered, with diving, Nitrox, national park fees, transfers and Starlink Wi-Fi in the nightly rate. For a family or a group of friends that keeps the sums simple.

Her published sample routes run 5 nights in Komodo, 7 nights in north and central Raja Ampat and 11 nights from Ambon through the Banda Islands to Misool and Sorong, so a group can match a route to the season and the time it has.

days.title: Labuan Bajo to the Sebayur islands
days.summary: Board in Labuan Bajo and sail to Sebayur Besar and Sebayur Kecil for diving, snorkelling, beach time and a trek if the tide allows. Dinner al fresco.

days.title: Gili Lawa Darat and Gili Lawa Laut
days.summary: Hike to the Gili Lawa lookout after breakfast, then kayak, paddleboard, snorkel or dive the sites around the islands.

days.title: Gili Banta
days.summary: A full day at Gili Banta with the yacht's beach set-up and diving nearby, then sundowners and a beach barbecue.

days.title: Manta Point, Karang Makassar, Padar
days.summary: Morning with the manta rays at Manta Point and the sandbar at Karang Makassar, then the trek to the top of Padar in the afternoon.

days.title: Pink Beach, Rinca, Kalong
days.summary: Beach time and diving at Pink Beach, then Komodo dragons on Rinca with a park ranger, and sundowners near Kalong.

days.title: Labuan Bajo
days.summary: Breakfast aboard, then the crew transfers you to the airport.

itineraries.name: 8 Days, 7 Nights North & Central Raja Ampat

days.title: Sorong
days.summary: Met at Sorong airport and transferred to the harbour, about 20 minutes. Lunch on deck as she sails for Raja Ampat, with a snorkel or check dive if time allows.

days.title: Kri Peninsula
days.summary: Snorkel the mangroves or kayak Mioskon Bay, dive the coral slopes off Kri, and go ashore at the village on Mansuar.

days.title: The Passage
days.summary: A dawn walk to a birdwatching platform for the red Paradisaea rubra, then the mushroom islands of Kabui Bay and the tidal channel of the Passage.

days.title: Penemu Islands
days.summary: The lookout trail over the limestone domes of Penemu, then snorkelling and diving with turtles, mantas and schooling fish.

days.title: Wayag
days.summary: Water sports and beach time in the Wayag karsts, with a climb to the peak for the view over the lagoons.

days.title: Wofoh
days.summary: Two islands joined by a shallow reef, for beachcombing, paddleboarding and a coral wall dive.

days.title: Arborek and Mansuar
days.summary: Dive or snorkel with the mantas off Arborek, visit the village, then cross to Sorong overnight.

days.title: Sorong
days.summary: Breakfast on deck and transfer to the airport.

itineraries.name: 12 Days, 11 Nights Spice Islands & Misool, Ambon to Sorong

days.title: Tulehu Bay and Molana
days.summary: Met by the crew and taken to Tulehu port to board, then an afternoon of snorkelling, diving and beach time at Molana island.

days.title: Saparua and Nusa Laut
days.summary: Dive the hard corals of Nusa Laut, then go ashore to Duurstede Fort, a post in the clove trade.

days.title: Suanggi and Banda Neira
days.summary: Dive or snorkel Pulau Suanggi with snapper, trevally and white-tip reef sharks, then arrive at Banda Neira.

days.title: Run, Neilaka and Ai
days.summary: Rumah Besi, an old Dutch nutmeg warehouse, and a nutmeg plantation under kenari trees, then diving between Neilaka and Run.

days.title: Banda Besar
days.summary: Fort Hollandia, built in 1674, and the nutmeg harvest, then an afternoon dive at Batu Hangus north of Gunung Api.

days.title: Hatta and Sahil
days.summary: A full day of water sports and the beach set-up around Hatta and Sahil, then east towards Koon.

days.title: Koon
days.summary: A small island east of Seram ringed by a protected reef; overnight crossing to Misool in the afternoon.

days.title: Misool
days.summary: Four days in south-east Misool, with dives at Boo Windows and Magic Mountain.

days.title: Misool
days.summary: The ancestral caves of Tomolol, with cave paintings and a swim through an orchid-hung cave.

days.title: Misool
days.summary: Channels, lagoons and beaches, with a nearby pearl farm.

days.title: Misool to Sorong
days.summary: A last day in Misool before she sails for Sorong.

days.title: Sorong
days.summary: Breakfast on deck and transfer to the airport.

faqs: How much does it cost to charter Celestia?

Celestia is chartered whole: US$13,500 a night plus VAT in 2026, US$14,000 in 2027 and US$15,000 in 2028, for up to 14 guests. Meals, house wine and local beer, diving with Nitrox, water toys, transfers, park fees and three massages a day are included. Fuel surcharges, other alcohol and crew gratuities are not.
Can we book a single cabin on Celestia?
No. Celestia publishes private charters only, for the whole yacht and its seven staterooms. For shared-cabin voyages in the same waters, look at Aliikai or the cabin voyages on Rascal and Rebel.
Where and when does Celestia sail?

Raja Ampat from October to April, Komodo, Sumbawa and Alor from May to September, and the Spice Islands in April and from September to October, as she moves between the two. The schedule is typical and can change.
How many guests does Celestia take?

Up to 14, in seven en-suite staterooms: a Master on the main deck, two Owner's staterooms with private terraces on the upper deck, and four Deluxe staterooms on the lower deck, two with queen beds and two with twins. A crew of 17 looks after them.
Yes. Dive equipment, a dive master and Nitrox for certified divers are in the charter rate. Dive certification, a dive computer and dive insurance are not.

No age limit is published and every stateroom sleeps two, with twin beds in two of the Deluxe staterooms. Families with young children have sailed her; the crew chose snorkelling spots close to shore for them.
A 50% non-refundable deposit at booking and the balance 60 days before departure.
